content.value: Use a library through its API; read signatures, preconditions, postconditions, return values, and side effects.

An application programming interface describes the operations a component exposes. A library packages reusable code. To use a method responsibly, read both its header and its behavioral description: what each argument means, which inputs are valid, whether the receiver changes, and what value comes back. You do not need the private implementation to use a stable contract.

Packages organize classes. An import allows use of a class name without its full package prefix; it does not create an object. Classes such as String and Math in java.lang are available automatically. Other classes, such as ArrayList and Scanner in java.util, commonly require imports.

The valid call has spaces = 13. Both arguments are int and satisfy the documented relationship. Capacity.remaining(5, 9) matches the types but violates the precondition, so the stated contract does not promise a useful result.

A matching signature is not enough to guarantee a valid call. Do not confuse import with construction, or void with a guarantee of no side effects. Read the return type and documentation before assigning a result.
Write a valid call that reports unused spaces when capacity is 30 and used is 12. Answer: Capacity.remaining(30, 12), yielding 18. Describe the boundary cases used = 0 and used = capacity.
